correctness.rationale: For every interior time the binary reading is unbiased by symmetry and the Bayes conditional mean is \(1/2+C(t)Y\). The classical uniform positive-occupation law gives \(\operatorname{Var}(Q)=1/12\). For a finite independent symmetric noise variable, the conditional sign response \(f_r(z)=\Pr(|N|<z/r)\) for almost every z>0 is nonnegative and nonincreasing in r. Conditional Gaussian integration makes the two-time binary sign correlation strictly increasing with the latent correlation. Under log-odds time the standardized Brownian-bridge correlation is \(e^{-|x-z|/2}\) and Lebesgue time has the even strictly unimodal logistic density; a Stieltjes layer-cake representation proves its convolution with any nonzero even decreasing correlation profile is uniquely maximized at log-odds zero. Standardized-noise dominance then yields strict unique midpoint optimality even for arbitrary discrete or heavy-tailed symmetric noise. Elementary integration proves the Gaussian-risk formula and the noiseless exact constants. The actual standalone verify.py executed successfully with 116 deterministic checks; finite checks are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The final claim is a distribution-free one-bit *location-design* theorem under an arbitrary symmetric noise law and an explicit standardized-noise condition, with a Gaussian finite-noise risk formula. Godrèche (2017) already establishes the unnoised bridge two-time sign correlation and the uniform occupation law; those are credited as inputs, and the integrated noiseless covariance alone is not presented as the novelty. Pozdnyakov et al. (2014) use multiple full-valued noisy Brownian observations, while Ivanovs–Podolskij (2020) and Altmeyer–Le Guével (2021) optimize high-frequency full-valued observation estimators. No inspected source implies the simultaneous one-bit, arbitrary-noise, unique-time theorem. Published mathematical-finding comparisons and prior accessible claim summaries did not yield coverage. A historical unindexed equivalence remains a risk; lack of a search hit is not used as a novelty proof.

value.rationale: The exact location problem is natural in bandwidth-limited measurement of stochastic occupation fractions: one bit is retained and the observation must be chosen before observing the path. The theorem gives an all-times optimum and exact finite-noise Gaussian Bayes risk, robust simultaneously to discrete and heavy-tailed symmetric errors and to both constant physical and standardized error scales. It quantifies an exact noiseless variance-reduction ceiling \(9-6\sqrt2\) and yields an explicit information-design rule, not just a numerical optimum or elementary type check. The strict logistic-convolution lemma is structurally central; scope excludes adaptive and general channels.
